title: Hosted API demo: embeddings & rerank - NovaSearch
summary: Hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking for improving search relevance. Demoed Redwood embeddings endpoint, vector storage/consumption pattern, and rerank endpoint. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, security (SOC 2, KMS), and POC benchmarks.
topics: Console demo: embedding dashboard + Optimize recommendations
Next steps: pricing, security docs, POC schedule
transcript: 00:00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for joining, looks like we got most folks. quick intro I'm Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Samir is our solutions engineer, Ana from product is here too. 00:00:10 Jared Cole: Hey thanks Lena, excited to see this. we are trying to improve our relevance for legal search, lots of short queries and long doc context. 00:00:20 Samir Patel: Awesome, we'll walk through the hosted API flow — embeddings generation, storing vectors, and then a small rerank step to improve ordering. I'll share my screen — lemme know if you can't see it. 00:00:35 Priya Nair: Screen's good. quick note, we are evaluating latency under 200ms for rerank in the a typical query path, and cost needs to be under our current budget which is about $0.02 per query on avg. 00:00:50 Samir Patel: Cool that's helpful, we'll show two patterns: 1) cheap approximate vector search with our embedding + nearest-neighbor store and 2) an optional rerank call that runs a low-latency model to reorder top-k results. 00:01:10 Marcus Lee: For compliance we need to know where data lives — any hosted EU + US options and is there KMS/HSM to manage keys? 00:01:20 Ana Gómez: Yes we support regional hosted endpoints, and KMS integrations. I'll drop the security whitepaper after the call. 00:01:30 Speaker 1: (inaudible) may also want to see SOC 2 and audit logs. 00:01:35 Lena Ortiz: Absolutely, we'll include SOC 2 and our audit log docs. ok Samir over to you for the demo. 00:01:45 Samir Patel: Alright starting with the API quickstart. endpoint is /v1/embeddings. payload: text -> vector. show example request in python and curl. 00:02:05 Samir Patel: we demo creating embeddings for a set of legal clauses, then we index vectors into a vector DB (we demo using Pinecone in this example but the same flow works with self-hosted or our managed vector index). 00:02:25 Priya Nair: quick question — do you do any normalization or sentencepiece issues that would change embeddings between model versions? we've seen drift. 00:02:35 Samir Patel: Good question — we version embeddings models. Canarying is possible via the Console and we expose model_id in the response so you can pin which model you use for indexing vs querying. some drift is unavoidable when switching families but our Optimize tool suggests quantization and model variants per workload. 00:02:55 00:03:05 Samir Patel: now the rerank endpoint — we take the original query + top-k candidate docs (you can send ids + context) and we return a score + re-ordered list. show API call: POST /v1/rerank with candidates payload. 00:03:25 Jared Cole: what's the typical latency for rerank? our 200ms SLO is pretty strict. 00:03:30 Samir Patel: On hosted we see 70-120ms med for small rerank models on typical 10-20 candidate sets; if you need <50ms we'd recommend dedicated capacity or a smaller rerank model. also batching and prefix caching help. 00:03:50 Ellen Park: And cost — do you charge per token for rerank or per request? 00:03:55 Lena Ortiz: For hosted API it's per-token for generation-style models and per-call for rerank endpoints (and we show token-equivalent pricing in the Console); we'll send an example price sheet. 00:04:10 Priya Nair: Any built-in evaluation tooling to compare baseline vs reranked results? ground truth relevance tests? 00:04:20 Ana Gómez: Yes within the Console we have an Eval set flow: upload labeled queries, run against different pipelines (emb-only vs emb+rerank), get precision/recall and side-by-side diffs. Optimize can recommend model/quantization to balance cost and accuracy. 00:04:40 Speaker 2: (crosstalk) how does the rerank get the document context, do you fetch the embeddings server-side? 00:04:45 Samir Patel: Usually you fetch top-k ids from your vector store and then either send the snippet text in the rerank request or include a cached embedding; we also support sending the vector and we can perform dot-product in our rerank pipeline if you want to avoid text payloads. 00:05:10 Marcus Lee: For our legal docs we often need entire sections, not just snippets. how does tokenization affect cost? 00:05:20 Samir Patel: Tokenization impacts cost directly for rerank if you send full contexts. common approach: send short snippets and let rerank score, if you need long context we recommend using our KV cache + prefix caching to reduce repeated tokens for frequent doc prefixes. Optimize will also flag high-cost prompts. 00:05:45 Jared Cole: Security follow-up: can we have VPC peering or a private deployment? we have PII in some documents. 00:05:55 Lena Ortiz: We offer Dedicated and Private deployments — Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and network isolation; Private is VPC/on-prem with customer-managed networking and KMS integrations. we'll include a short matrix comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private. 00:06:15 Priya Nair: Also curious about auditability — can we get per-request trace and token-level cost breakdown? 00:06:25 Ana Gómez: Yes Console exposes token-level cost breakdown and tracing hooks, and we can stream audit logs to your SIEM or S3. 00:06:35 Samir Patel: switching back to demo — here's a sample response: top 10 nearest neighbors, then we call rerank and you see ordering change, we show the score delta. 00:06:50 Samir Patel: note — the transcript and some product names might be mis-typed in the recording, apologies if email references look odd. 00:07:05 Jared Cole: This looks promising. how long to spin up a POC? we want realistic benchmark against our 1M doc index. 00:07:15 Samir Patel: For a hosted POC we can provision a test key and run a benchmark week; typically we pipeline a sample of 100k docs for initial numbers then scale to 1M. if you need guaranteed throughput we can propose Dedicated. 00:07:35 Marcus Lee: One more — competitors. we're also looking at Elastic and Algolia and evaluating OpenAI for embeddings. wondering on differentiation. 00:07:45 Lena Ortiz: Redwood differentiators: production-first runtime, unified tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and Optimize recommendations for cost/quality. plus rollouts and automatic fallback policies to keep apps online. 00:08:05 Priya Nair: Are there any known gotchas migrating from OpenAI embeddings? vector dims mismatch or minor scoring changes? 00:08:15 Samir Patel: There can be differences in vector space. we recommend reindexing for a model switch and run a small A/B. Console's Eval flow automates much of that. 00:08:30 Ellen Park: Could you show how Optimize suggests batching settings? 00:08:35 Ana Gómez: Sure — Optimize analyzes your per-route token length distribution and recommends a batching window and quantization for lower-cost model variants while preserving accuracy on labeled evals. here's a sample suggestion panel. 00:09:10 Jared Cole: ok great, let's talk timeline. we're aiming to have a decision by end of Jan and start a POC mid-Feb. 00:09:20 Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. recap: we'll send pricing and dedicated capacity options, security whitepaper and SOC 2, and sample benchmark scripts. we'll propose POC week starting Feb 15. 00:09:35 Samir Patel: Action item — I'll prepare a sample rerank benchmark script and run a smoke test against your sample queries if you can share a small dataset. 00:09:50 Priya Nair: We can share a sanitized subset this week. 00:09:55 Marcus Lee: Also send a matrix for data residency and KMS options. 00:10:05 Lena Ortiz: Will do. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. 00:10:15 Speaker 3: bye all. 00:10:20 [call ended]
